title: From Opinion: Nikole Hannah-Jones and Ta-Nehisi Coates on the Story We Tell About America

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分采访内容，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hi, daily listeners.
sentences.zh: 你好，各位每日听众。

sentences.en: I'm Ezra Klein, an opinion columnist at The New York Times and host of The Ezra Klein Show,
sentences.zh: 我是埃兹拉·克莱因，《纽约时报》的观点专栏作家，也是《埃兹拉·克莱因秀》的主持人，

sentences.en: where I have conversations with fascinating people whose ideas are shaping our lives or should be.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我与那些思想正在塑造我们生活（或者本应塑造我们生活）的迷人人物进行对话。

sentences.en: Today, I wanted to share with you an interview I did with the writer Ta-Nehisi Coates and The Times' own Nicole Hannah-Jones.
sentences.zh: 今天，我想与大家分享我与作家塔-内西·科茨以及《纽约时报》自己的妮可·汉娜-琼斯进行的一次采访。

sentences.en: We covered the backlash to the 1619 Project, the fight over how we tell and who gets to tell the story of American history,
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了对“1619项目”的强烈抵制，关于我们如何讲述美国历史以及谁有权讲述这段历史的争论，

sentences.en: the nature of American democracy, how we should teach journalism, the nonfiction they love, and so much more.
sentences.zh: 美国民主的本质、我们应该如何教授新闻学、他们喜爱的非虚构作品等等。

sentences.en: So enjoy the interview.
sentences.zh: 那么，请欣赏这次采访。

sentences.en: And if you like it, subscribe to The Ezra Klein Show wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢，请在你获取播客的任何地方订阅《埃兹拉·克莱因秀》。

sentences.en: My guests today need a little introduction.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾无需多做介绍。

sentences.en: Nicole Hannah-Jones is an award-winning investigative journalist for The New York Times Magazine, where she led the 1619 Project.
sentences.zh: 妮可·汉娜-琼斯是《纽约时报杂志》屡获殊荣的调查记者，她在那里领导了“1619项目”。

sentences.en: She won a Pulitzer Prize for the lead essay in that.
sentences.zh: 她凭借该项目的主打文章获得了普利策奖。

sentences.en: She's also done amazing work over the years on racial inequality and segregation in the American education system.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她在种族不平等和美国教育体系中的种族隔离问题上也做了出色的工作。

sentences.en: Ta-Nehisi Coates, of course, is the author of the National Book Award winner Between the World and Me,
sentences.zh: 塔-内西·科茨当然是美国国家图书奖获奖作品《在世界与我之间》的作者，

sentences.en: the Oprah Book Club pick, The Water Dancer, essays like The Case for Reparations, Marvel Comics, like Captain America and Black Panther.
sentences.zh: 奥普拉读书俱乐部选书《水舞者》的作者，也是《赔偿的理由》等文章的作者，还创作过漫威漫画，如《美国队长》和《黑豹》。

sentences.en: And now he's writing the next Superman movie.
sentences.zh: 现在他正在撰写下一部超人电影的剧本。

sentences.en: So he's a busy guy.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个大忙人。

sentences.en: They're both busy, but the official reason for this conversation is they're adding another affiliation.
sentences.zh: 他们都很忙，但这次对话的官方原因是他们正在增加一个新的身份。

sentences.en: Both of them are taking faculty positions at Howard University.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都将在霍华德大学担任教职。

sentences.en: In Hannah-Jones' case, this comes after the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, initially recommended her for position,
sentences.zh: 就汉娜-琼斯而言，这是在北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校最初推荐她担任该职位之后发生的，

sentences.en: but then over the objections of the faculty, the university's board of trustees denied her tenure
sentences.zh: 但随后在教职员工的反对下，该大学的董事会拒绝了她的终身教职，

sentences.en: because, as best as we can tell, some of them were uncomfortable with the 1619 Project.
sentences.zh: 因为据我们所知，他们中的一些人对“1619项目”感到不安。

sentences.en: Then under more political pressure, the University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, reversed that decision and tried to offer her tenure.
sentences.zh: 后来在更多的政治压力下，北卡罗来纳大学教堂山分校推翻了这一决定，并试图向她提供终身教职。

sentences.en: But Hannah-Jones decided to go to Howard.
sentences.zh: 但汉娜-琼斯决定去霍华德大学。

sentences.en: And so the conversation begins in what Hannah-Jones and Coates are trying to build at Howard.
sentences.zh: 因此，对话从汉娜-琼斯和科茨试图在霍华德大学建立的东西开始。

sentences.en: But the conversation revolves around a topic that they've both wrestled with across their careers.
sentences.zh: 但对话围绕着他们两人在职业生涯中都曾努力解决的一个话题展开。

sentences.en: How to understand and teach America's history.
sentences.zh: 如何理解和教授美国的历史。

sentences.en: You have heard plenty by now about the fights over critical race theory, about teaching the 1619 Project, the bills that are passing in different Republican states on those issues.
sentences.zh: 关于批判性种族理论的争论、关于教授“1619项目”的争论，以及不同共和党州正在通过的关于这些议题的法案，你现在已经听得够多了。

sentences.en: I'm interested here in the fight behind that fight.
sentences.zh: 我在这里感兴趣的是那场争论背后的争论。

sentences.en: Why this battle over American history now?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在会出现这场关于美国历史的斗争？

sentences.en: On some level, who cares?
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Why is there so much more electricity over how we understand our past than how we describe our present?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们对如何理解过去的热情，远高于对如何描述现在的关注？

sentences.en: What are the stakes?
sentences.zh: 赌注是什么？

sentences.en: What changes when the story a country tells about itself changes?
sentences.zh: 当一个国家讲述关于自身的历史发生改变时，会发生什么变化？

sentences.en: What changes when who has the power to tell that story changes?
sentences.zh: 当谁有权讲述这段历史发生改变时，又会发生什么变化？

sentences.en: And why is now the moment for this collision?
sentences.zh: 为什么现在是这场碰撞的时刻？

sentences.en: So that conversation takes us to all sorts of places.
sentences.zh: 所以这次对话带我们去了各种各样的地方。

sentences.en: The 1619 Project and the backlash to it, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有“1619项目”及其引发的强烈抵制。

sentences.en: The cracked foundations of American democracy.
sentences.zh: 美国民主的裂痕。

sentences.en: The political uses of American exceptionalism.
sentences.zh: 美国例外论的政治用途。

sentences.en: Whether patriotism can coexist with realism and even regret.
sentences.zh: 爱国主义是否能与现实主义甚至遗憾共存。

sentences.en: The relationship between Barack Obama and Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 巴拉克·奥巴马和唐纳德·特朗普之间的关系。

sentences.en: And then at the end, we widen out to the work of journalism, to the craft of writing, to the toxicity of Twitter, the nonfiction they love,
sentences.zh: 最后，我们扩展到新闻工作、写作技巧、推特的毒性、他们喜爱的非虚构作品，

sentences.en: the lessons children and students teach us, and much more.
sentences.zh: 孩子们和学生教给我们的课程，以及更多内容。

sentences.en: As always, my email is reclineshow at nytimes.com.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我的邮箱是 reclineshow@nytimes.com。

sentences.en: Nicole Anna Jones, Ta-Nehisi Coates, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 妮可·汉娜-琼斯，塔-内西·科茨，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我们。

sentences.en: So, this conversation has a news peg, which is that you're both going to take faculty positions at Howard University in the fall.
sentences.zh: 那么，这次对话有一个新闻切入点，那就是你们两人秋季都将去霍华德大学担任教职。

sentences.en: And so, Ta-Nehisi, let me start with the why here.
sentences.zh: 所以，塔-内西，让我从“为什么”开始问起。

sentences.en: When you write or say anything at this point, you have an audience now of hundreds of thousands of people, often millions of people.
sentences.zh: 当你现在写下或说出任何话时，你已经拥有了成千上万，甚至往往是数百万的受众。

sentences.en: So, why put the energy into teaching single classrooms at a time?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么要投入精力去一次只教一个教室的学生呢？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, putting aside the fact that I think the craft of writing is very, very important, that it has a significant role in a functioning democracy,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，抛开我认为写作技巧非常非常重要，它在运作良好的民主国家中发挥着重要作用这一点不谈，

sentences.en: putting aside just enjoying the company of young people, you know, and the music that they listen to and, you know, what they think is cool and how, you know,
sentences.zh: 抛开仅仅享受与年轻人在一起的时光，你知道，听他们听的音乐，你知道，他们认为什么是酷的，以及他们如何，你知道，

sentences.en: they keep my mind young.
sentences.zh: 他们让我的思想保持年轻。

sentences.en: There is the fact of when you write or you practice any sort of craft for a long period of time, a kind of muscle memory takes over.
sentences.zh: 事实是，当你长期写作或从事任何一种手艺时，一种肌肉记忆就会接管一切。

sentences.en: It has to, you know, you have to stop thinking about things after a while.
sentences.zh: 它必须这样，你知道，过了一段时间你就必须停止思考这些事情。

sentences.en: You have to just kind of do them.
sentences.zh: 你必须只是去做它们。

sentences.en: I find it to be an incredible intellectual exercise to have to effectively re-engineer and explain to a novice why a piece of, you know, journalism that you really,
sentences.zh: 我发现，必须有效地重新设计并向新手解释为什么一篇你非常、非常欣赏的新闻报道能够奏效，这是一种令人难以置信的智力锻炼。

sentences.en: really admire works.
sentences.zh: 而且不能仅仅退回到“它真的很好”这种说法。

sentences.en: And not to be able to just retreat to, it's just really good.
sentences.zh: 我总是告诉我的学生，你知道，我们生活在一个人们除了读你的文章之外还可以做各种各样事情的时代。

sentences.en: I always tell my students, you know, we live in a time wherein people could be doing all sorts of things besides reading you.
sentences.zh: 你在和智能手机竞争。

sentences.en: You're in competition with a smartphone.
sentences.zh: 你在和游戏机竞争。

sentences.en: You're in competition with a video game console.
sentences.zh: 你在和，你知道，HBO Max、苹果以及此时此刻各种各样的流媒体选项竞争。

sentences.en: You're in competition with, you know, HBO Max and Apple and all sorts of streaming options at this point.
sentences.zh: 你必须带着一种紧迫感去写作。

sentences.en: You have to write with a sense of immediacy.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，教授这一点，你知道，向年轻人传授这一课，特别是在这个时刻，是非常、非常、非常重要的。

sentences.en: And so I think there's something really, really, really important about teaching that, about, you know, imparting that lesson to young people, especially at this moment.
sentences.zh: 同时，我认为这对我有好处。

sentences.en: And at the same time, I think it's good for me.
sentences.zh: 我认为这样做实际上对我自己有好处。

sentences.en: I think it's actually good for me to do that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢关于竞争的那一点。

sentences.en: And I love that point about competition.
sentences.zh: 当我经营 Vox 时，人们总是问我关于竞争对手的问题，说，你知道，538 网站。

sentences.en: Back when I ran Vox, people would always ask me about my competition and say, you know, 538.
sentences.zh: 或者我说，不，不，不，如果有人读 538，他们也会读我们的。

sentences.en: Or I said, no, no, no, if somebody reads 538, they're going to read us.
sentences.zh: 我的竞争对手是 Xbox，对吧？

sentences.en: My competition is Xbox, right?
sentences.zh: 我必须让你从那些客观上比读我们的文章有趣得多的事情中抽身出来。

sentences.en: I got to get you from things that are objectively a lot more fun to do than read us.
sentences.zh: 这给作者带来了很大的压力。

sentences.en: And like, it's a lot of weight on the writer.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才在开头说了一些话，说写作与功能性民主之间存在联系。

sentences.en: But you said something right at the beginning of that, that there's a connection between writing and a functional democracy.
sentences.zh: 妮可，你正在那里建立一个新闻与民主中心。

sentences.en: And Nicole, you're building a journalism and democracy center there.
sentences.zh: 所以告诉我关于它的愿景，特别是你所强调的新闻与民主之间的联系。

sentences.en: So tell me about the vision for it and particularly the journalism democracy connection you're drawing.
sentences.zh: 为什么不仅仅是一个新闻中心？

sentences.en: Why not just a journalism center?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我一直认为，拥有那些职责是告知公众，同时也让当权者负责的人，对于拥有一个运作良好的民主国家至关重要。

sentences.en: Well, I've always believed that having people whose job it is to inform the public, but also to hold powerful people to account is critical to have a functioning democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是我实际上与这个国家的开国元勋们保持一致的一个领域，他们认为如果你没有受过关于政客教育的公民，你就无法拥有民主。

sentences.en: This is one area where I'm actually aligned with this nation's founders who believed that you could not have a democracy if you didn't have citizens who were educated about the politicians.
sentences.zh: 他们将要投票支持的人，以及他们将要支持的政策。

sentences.en: They were going to be voting for and about the policies that they were going to be supporting.
sentences.zh: 作为一个也花了很多时间研究黑人媒体特殊作用的美国黑人，我认为你无法将这两件事分开。

sentences.en: And as a Black American who's also spent a lot of time studying the very particular role of the Black press, I think that you just can't disentangle these two things.
sentences.zh: 如果我们的媒体不是以一种诚实的方式，以一种触及真相且不仅仅是速记的方式来报道我们国家的政治，

sentences.en: That if our press is not covering the politics of our country in a way that is honest, in a way that gets to the truth and is more than stenography,
sentences.zh: 那么我们的民主就不可能健康。

sentences.en: then our democracy can't be healthy.
sentences.zh: 历史上充满了这样的例子。

sentences.en: And history is littered with examples of that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看看主流媒体在民权运动初期是如何报道的。

sentences.en: We can look at how mainstream media covered the civil rights movement at its beginning.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看看主流媒体是如何报道重建时期，然后是救赎时期，以及媒体的失败，

sentences.en: We can look at how mainstream media covered reconstruction and then redemption and the failures of the press and the press,
sentences.zh: 主流媒体站在白人至上主义一边，这正是随后创造并传播了导致我们民主失败的叙事的原因。

sentences.en: mainstream press siding with white supremacy is what then creates the narrative and passes along the narrative that allows for our democracy to fail.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们现在正处于我们国家另一个关键时刻，我们的国家正处于某种事物的边缘，我们还不知道会走向哪个方向。

sentences.en: So I think we are in another pivotal moment right now in our country where our country is on the cusp of something, which direction we go, we don't yet know.
sentences.zh: 但我认为新闻业并没有像它需要的那样应对这一局面。

sentences.en: But I don't think that journalism is rising to the occasion as it needs to be.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一名记者，我的使命的一部分，

sentences.en: And so part of my mission as a journalist,
sentences.zh: 我最初想要成为记者的原因，就是为了真正代表那些在这个国家没有权力的人而战。

sentences.en: the reason I ever wanted to become a journalist in the first place was to really fight on behalf of those who don't wield power in this country.
sentences.zh: 而那种制衡体系失灵了。

sentences.en: And that system of checks and balances is off.
sentences.zh: 媒体是我们民主的防火墙。

sentences.en: The press is the firewall of our democracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为那道防火墙现在并没有守住。

sentences.en: And I think that firewall is not holding right now.
sentences.zh: 还有什么地方比培养下一代记者更能加强这一点呢？他们将进入新闻编辑室，

sentences.en: And what better place to bolster that than to train up the next generation of journalists who are going to be going into newsrooms,
sentences.zh: 希望他们能配备适当的工具，去做新闻业在这一刻需要做的事情。

sentences.en: hopefully armed with the proper tools to do what journalism needs to do in this moment.
sentences.zh: 我认为谈论种族与民主的这种联系非常、非常重要。

sentences.en: I think it's really, really important to talk about that nexus of race and democracy.
sentences.zh: 我认为现在正在发生的事情之一是，如果你考虑到这样一个事实：在这个国家历史的大部分时间里，黑人都被排除在政治主体之外。

sentences.en: I think one of the things that's happening right now, if you consider the fact that for most of this country's history, Black people have been written out of the body politic.
sentences.zh: 我们有重建时期的实验，我们也有民权运动后开始的实验。

sentences.en: We have the experiment of reconstruction and we have the experiment that began in the post-civil rights movement.
sentences.zh: 但即使在民权运动后的大部分时间里，你知道，斗争一直在于，你知道，获得准入权，而且现在仍然是，你知道，进入投票站的准入权。

sentences.en: But even for most of the post-civil rights movement, you know, the fight has been, you know, in terms of getting access and still is, you know, access to the ballot box.
sentences.zh: 那正是重建时期的斗争，你知道。

sentences.en: And that was the fight, you know, during reconstruction.
sentences.zh: 我想说，这个时刻在非裔美国作家和记者能够获得他们过去无法获得的扩音器方面是独一无二的。

sentences.en: I would say that this moment is singular in terms of African-American writers and journalists having access to the kind of megaphones that they have had access to compared to in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 当我在霍华德大学读书时，“1619项目”简直是不可想象的。

sentences.en: When I was a student at Howard, a 1619 project was just unimaginable.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》竟然会把编辑权交给像妮可这样的人，是不可想象的。

sentences.en: It was unimaginable that the New York Times would actually hand over editorship to someone like Nicole.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是，你知道，一位黑人记者，而是一位会，你知道，提出对这个国家起源完全不同想象的黑人记者。

sentences.en: Not just, you know, a Black journalist, but a Black journalist who would, you know, posit a very different imagining of this country's origins.
sentences.zh: 她会，你知道，然后召集各种记者、作家和诗人，你知道，他们自己来参与。

sentences.en: That she would, you know, then convene various journalists and writers and poets, you know, themselves to come in.
sentences.zh: 那是一种根本不会发生的项目。

sentences.en: And that was the kind of project that just didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我认为过去10年里发生了一些事情，我想大概是10多年了，

sentences.en: And I think something that's happened in the past 10 years is there have been, and I guess a little more than 10 years,
sentences.zh: 但我真的认为这是，你知道，奥巴马当选的反映。
